eventMetadata.context_description: Traders assign near-certain probability to a daily high of 26 °C or higher in Jinan on 24 August 2026 because late-summer climatology and real-time forecasts place the maximum well above that threshold. Jinan’s August average high is approximately 30–31 °C, driven by persistent subtropical high pressure, southerly flow, and high humidity that limits nocturnal cooling. The only realistic way the market could resolve below 26 °C would be an unforecasted, rapid influx of markedly cooler maritime or frontal air—an event with negligible support in current numerical guidance and inconsistent with the observed thermal environment.

**Forecast consensus from the National Weather Service and other models points to a high near 79–81°F in Chicago on August 25, 2026, under mostly sunny to partly cloudy skies with southerly winds of 5–10 mph.** This aligns with the market’s heaviest weighting on the 80–81°F bin (50.5%) and 78–79°F bin (32.0%), as current conditions feature stable high pressure, modest warm advection from the south, and typical late-summer insolation without strong synoptic forcing or extreme boundary-layer heating.

Lake Michigan’s moderating influence keeps shoreline readings from spiking higher, while inland areas may briefly touch the upper end of the favored range. No heat dome, dry downslope flow, or rapid model shifts have emerged in the latest runs to push probabilities toward 82°F+ or sub-78°F outcomes. Historical averages (around 82°F) and recent August 2026 observations (mostly 77–82°F) further anchor expectations in the narrow 78–81°F window.

Traders appear to be pricing the low uncertainty in short-range guidance, with the market-implied odds reflecting the narrow spread typical of well-resolved warm-season forecasts this close to the event.

eventMetadata.context_description: NWS forecasts peg Tuesday's Denver high at 88°F under mostly sunny skies, with only a 30% chance of afternoon thunderstorms after 4pm, aligning with the market's tight clustering around the 86–89°F bins. This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 26 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rpll

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus reflects significant uncertainty between 31°C and 32°C as Manila’s likely daily maximum on August 26, with both outcomes holding roughly 30% implied probability amid the southwest monsoon’s variable influence. Official PAGASA guidance and regional model runs show scattered showers and high humidity expected to limit daytime heating, while reduced cloud cover or lighter winds could allow brief spikes toward the upper threshold. Historical late-August baselines average near 31°C, but urban heat island effects and short-term shifts in the monsoon trough introduce forecast spread that traders are pricing closely. Updated model guidance and local observations over the next 48 hours will likely clarify whether precipitation suppresses or permits the higher reading.
